info.title: Timetastic API
info.description:
# Introduction

👏 Welcome to the Timetastic API 👏

You can use the Timetastic API to integrate Timetastic into other software applications and custom workflows.

The API is designed to be a predictable and intuitive way to interact with your company’s Timetastic account.

Like Timetastic itself, the API is under continuous development, so changes and improvements are to be expected. Be sure to keep an eye on our [Twitter Changelog](https://twitter.com/search?f=tweets&vertical=default&q=timetastic%20%23changelog&src=typd) to receive information on new additions and changes to both Timetastic and the API when we release new features and changes.

**Get started quickly:**

There's an OpenAPI specification at the top of this document so you can get set up and testing early and easily. You can import this collection into [Postman](https://www.postman.com/), [Insomnia](https://insomnia.rest/), [Paw](https://paw.cloud/) or your HTTP/Rest client of choice.

**Get stuck in:** Read the sections below on Authentication and Rate Limiting, then see what you can do!

# Rate Limiting

To keep things running smoothly, there is a rate limit of 5 requests per second, per API key.

If you exceed the limit, you'll get a `429` response code.

For successful calls, we set response headers containing information about the rate limit—which can help you monitor your usage.

**Monitoring Usage**

For calls that don't get rate limited, you can monitor your usage with the following headers:

- `X-Rate-Limit-Limit`: The rate limit period (e.g., 1s, 1m)
- `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining`: Number of requests remaining
- `X-Rate-Limit-Reset`: UTC date time (ISO 8601) when the limit resets

# Authentication

To use the API, you need an API token. Only admin users have access to an API token.

You can get or renew your API token from Timetastic: [https://app.timetastic.co.uk/api](https://app.timetastic.co.uk/api)

_The token identifies your user, so you'll have the same permissions as your user account._

## Example

To authorize, use this code:

```bash
curl "https://app.timetastic.co.uk/api/users" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
```

Replace `YOUR_TOKEN` with your API key.


## Big integrations / building us into your product?
Great! We're happy to have you. We'd love it if you could do us a huge favour and include either the
`User-Agent` header (for example, `User-Agent: YourApp/1.0`) or an `X-Client-ID` header (for example,
`X-Client-ID: YourApp`) telling us the product/app name so we can see who and how people are using the API.
It's just for metrics and seeing how popular/well used the API is. Thanks!  ❤️ (Also we have a referral programme so you might want to check that out too: https://timetastic.co.uk/rewards/)

get.summary: Get a chronological list of absences
get.description: Find out "who is off" on a certain day or range of days - whether thats public holidays, bookings, non working days or other events. Bookings are returned with times matching the user's work schedule so a multiple day booking will show start and end times for that day even if the booking covers multiple days Limited to 31 days per query. Rate limited to 1 request per second.

parameters.name: AbsenceQueryType
parameters.description: AllEvents: Returns Bookings, Non working days, Public Holidays, Locked Dates, Birthdays and Work anniversaries. AllAbsences: Returns everything we consider an absence: Bookings, Public Holidays and Non working days Bookings: Returns Bookings only PublicHolidays: returns Public Holidays only - `0` — **AllEvents**: Locked dates, birthdays, work anniversaries, absences, non working days, public holidays, everything on the wallchart basically - `1` — **AllAbsences**: Just absences - non-working days, public holidays, bookings - `2` — **Bookings**: Just bookings - `3` — **PublicHolidays**: Just public holidays

schema.description: AllEvents: Returns Bookings, Non working days, Public Holidays, Locked Dates, Birthdays and Work anniversaries. AllAbsences: Returns everything we consider an absence: Bookings, Public Holidays and Non working days Bookings: Returns Bookings only PublicHolidays: returns Public Holidays only - `0` — **AllEvents**: Locked dates, birthdays, work anniversaries, absences, non working days, public holidays, everything on the wallchart basically - `1` — **AllAbsences**: Just absences - non-working days, public holidays, bookings - `2` — **Bookings**: Just bookings - `3` — **PublicHolidays**: Just public holidays

400.description: If the start and end dates are invalid. Check the end is after the start date and that they don't cover more than 31 days

post.description:
Adds a new department using the settings provided in the model.
            
A rejection returns an `ErrorStatus` and an `ErrorMessage`. `NotPermitted` means the `managerId` is not a
user in your organisation, or has no email address. `InvalidValue` and `Failed` mean the department itself
was rejected — check `ErrorMessage`.
            
Model validation fails before any of that, and returns a different 400 body: an object keyed by
field name, each holding an array of messages. Check for `ErrorStatus` to tell the two apart.

400.description: The department could not be created.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

post.description:
As with the user edit endpoint - pass only the fields you want to update and we'll only update those.
            
A rejection returns an `ErrorStatus` and an `ErrorMessage`. `NotPermitted` means the department does not
exist or belongs to another organisation, or you are not allowed to edit it. `NothingToDo` means the
request produced no change. `InvalidValue` and `Failed` mean a supplied value was rejected — check
`ErrorMessage`.
            
Model validation fails before any of that, and returns a different 400 body: an object keyed by
field name, each holding an array of messages. Check for `ErrorStatus` to tell the two apart.

post.description: Update a holiday. You can use this to : 1) Approve a pending holiday 2) Decline a pending holiday 3) Cancel a holiday Note: This will raise a Webhook event if you have Webhooks configured. Important: an action that is refused still returns 200. Check `approvalResult` in the response body rather than relying on the status code. Its values are: - `Success` — the action was applied. - `AlreadyActioned` — the holiday has already been approved, declined or cancelled. - `DoesntExist` — the holiday could not be found when the action was applied. - `NotAllowed` — you are not allowed to perform that action on this holiday. - `UnknownError` — the action failed, or no recognised `holidayUpdateAction` was supplied. `message` carries a human readable version of the same thing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the holiday / a holiday token

parameters.name: holidayUpdateAction
parameters.description: The action you want to perform to the holiday

requestBody.description: options for reasons and suppressing notifications

200.description: The request was processed. Check `approvalResult` in the body — this is also returned when the action was refused.

400.description:
The body is a plain string. `"Holiday not found"` when no holiday matches the ID or token, and
`"You don't have permission"` when you cannot manage that user. You may cancel your own holiday without
managing rights, but only while it is still in the future.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

429.description: The overall API rate limit was exceeded.

get.description:
Query the holidays for your organisation.
There are many ways to filter the results, all of which are optional.
Results are limited to 100 per request.
            
Results are scoped to your organisation, so a filter that matches nothing — including an id
belonging to another organisation — returns an empty list rather than an error. Note the scope is
your organisation rather than your own visibility, so this can return absences for people you would
not see on a wallchart.

parameters.name: DepartmentId
parameters.description: Filter holidays by a department

parameters.name: LeaveTypeId
parameters.description: Filter holidays by a leave type

parameters.name: DepartmentManagersOnly
parameters.description: Filter holidays for those for department managers only

parameters.name: MyTeamOnly
parameters.description: Filter holidays for those for my team only, based on the user ID you set here.

parameters.name: MyFavouritesOnly
parameters.description: Filter holidays for those for my favourite users only, based on the User Id you set here.

parameters.name: UserIds
parameters.description: Filter holidays to include only these user(s)

parameters.name: ExclusionUserIds
parameters.description: Filter holidays to exclude these user(s)

parameters.name: NonArchivedUsersOnly
parameters.description: Only return holidays for users that haven't been archived

parameters.name: Start
parameters.description: Filter all holidays on or after this date

parameters.name: TransactionYear
parameters.description: Filter all holidays in this transaction year. Don't use this if you're not including the transactions in your query.

parameters.name: End
parameters.description: Filter all holidays before and including this date

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description:
Filter all holidays for the given status. If none given then all pending and approved holidays are included.
Values are: 
Pending = 1, Approved = 2, Cancelled = 4, Declined = 8
This is a bitwise enum, so for example if you want all declined and cancelled you can pass 12 as the status.

parameters.name: ApproverId
parameters.description: Filter holidays by the approver

parameters.name: PageNumber
parameters.description: Current page number, if required. Will default to 1 if not supplied

200.description: The matching holidays. An empty list if nothing matched the filter.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

post.description: Use this to submit a leave request to Timetastic. Depending on your authorisation, you can book for yourself, any other user at your organisation, your department, or the entire organisation. Note: This will raise a Webhook event if you have Webhooks configured. Important: a booking that is refused still returns 200. Always check `success` in the response body rather than relying on the status code. When `success` is `false`, `response` explains why. Reasons include: the dates contain no working days for that user, the request is zero length, the end date is before the start date, the user is already off for some of those dates, the user has insufficient allowance (or insufficient accrued allowance), the leave type is not active or its limit has been exceeded, the dates fall before the user's start date or after their end date, the dates are too far in the future, the leave year's allowance has not been created yet, a maximum-off limit would be breached, or the dates are locked. Three of those refusals can be retried with an override, and are flagged separately so you can prompt for confirmation. Resubmit with the matching request field set to book anyway — each one requires the appropriate permission: - `overrideRequired` (a maximum-off limit) → resubmit with `override` - `overrideLockedDateRequired` (a locked date) → resubmit with `overrideLockedDays` - `overrideAccruedAllowanceRequired` (accrued allowance) → resubmit with `overrideAccruedAllowance` When booking for a department or the whole organisation, `rejections` indicates that some users in the group could not be booked; `response` summarises which.

200.description: The request was processed. Check `success` in the body — this is also returned when the booking was refused.

400.description:
The request itself was malformed. The body is a plain string. Returned when the request could not be read,
and when a non-administrator tried to book for everyone.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

429.description: The overall API rate limit was exceeded.

post.description:
Use this to archive a user from Timetastic. They will be immediately logged out and unable to log in.
            
This endpoint is limited to 2 requests per second. An `archiveDate` must be supplied in the body.

400.description: The user could not be archived. `errorStatus` says why.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

403.description: The authenticated user is not an administrator.

429.description: The endpoint limit of 2 requests per second was exceeded.

post.description:
Use this to restore a user from Timetastic's Archive - they will be able to log in and use Timetastic as normal.
            
This endpoint is limited to 2 requests per second.
            
On success the body contains `wasEmailInUse`. When this is `true` the user was restored without their
original email address, because another active user has since taken it — set a new email address with
the edit endpoint before they can log in.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the user to restore

200.description: The user was restored, e.g. `{ "wasEmailInUse": false }`.

400.description: The user could not be restored. `errorStatus` says why.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

403.description: The authenticated user is not an administrator.

429.description: The endpoint limit of 2 requests per second was exceeded.

post.description:
Edits an existing user in Timetastic. Allows you to populate more data into a user record after an
initial ADD operation. You can pass any combination of the following parameters and only those values
will be changed.
            
This endpoint is limited to 2 requests per second.
            
Attempts that supply an email address already in use are counted against your organisation. The
count is shared with the add endpoint, and after 10 of them both start returning 429. The
count expires 24 hours after the *first* failure, not the last, and succeeding in the meantime
does not clear it. Check for an existing user before retrying rather than letting these
accumulate.

200.description: The user was updated.

400.description: The edit was rejected. `errorStatus` says why.

401.description:
The change was not permitted — `errorStatus` says why. An unauthenticated request also returns
401, but with no body at all.

403.description: The authenticated user is not an administrator.

429.description:
Too many recent requests supplied an email address that was already in use. Exceeding the endpoint
limit of 2 requests per second also returns 429, but as a plain text message from the rate limiter
rather than this body.

post.description:
Adds a new user to Timetastic, optionally triggering a welcome email.
            
This endpoint is limited to 2 requests per second.
            
Attempts that supply an email address already in use are counted against your organisation. The
count is shared with the edit endpoint, and after 10 of them both start returning 429. The
count expires 24 hours after the *first* failure, not the last, and succeeding in the meantime
does not clear it. Check for an existing user before retrying rather than letting these
accumulate.

200.description: The user was created. Returns the ID of the new user, e.g. `{ "id": 1234 }`.

400.description: The user could not be created. `errorStatus` says why.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

403.description: The authenticated user is not an administrator.

429.description:
Too many recent requests supplied an email address that was already in use. Note the reason is
carried in `result` rather than `errorStatus`. Exceeding the endpoint limit of 2 requests per
second also returns 429, but as a plain text message from the rate limiter rather than this body.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

403.description: You are not an administrator, your organisation is not on the Pro plan, or you are not allowed to view that user.

404.description: No user exists with that ID.

patch.summary: Assign public holidays to a user
patch.description:
Use when you want to assign a set of public holidays to a user.  Will turn public holidays on for this user if they are not already.
           If you pick a country/region code that's already in use by your organisation (which may have customisations from Timetastic's UI) - that set will be used
           If you pick a country/region that's not already in use by your organisation you'll get the standard public holidays for that region.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's ID in Timetastic

requestBody.description: The country and (optional) region codes to assign.

200.description: The public holiday set was assigned, or the user already had it.

400.description:
The request was rejected. This response has no body. It is returned when the body is missing or has no
`countryCode`, when the country/region code is not recognised, when the user ID does not exist or belongs
to another organisation, and when you are not allowed to manage that user.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

get.description:
Get a list of the recent Webhook items (defaults to the last day).
The dashboard will show events raised in the last day.
Timetastic retains 30 days of Webhook event history and you can access this via the API.
            
`daysHistory` is optional and defaults to 1. It is capped at 30 — a larger value is silently
reduced rather than rejected.

200.description: The recent webhook events. An empty list if there were none in that window.

401.description: The request was not authenticated — the API token is missing or invalid.

403.description: The authenticated user is not an administrator.

post.description:
This is an example of the payload you'll receive when we make a webhook request to your server.
Anything other than a 2xx response will be treated as a failure and redirects will not be followed.
            
This entry documents the payload we send to *you*. It is not a callable Timetastic endpoint.

200.description:
The shape of the payload we POST to your webhook URL. Shown for reference only; this endpoint
never returns it.

404.description: Always. There is nothing to call here.

absenceType.description:
Whether it's an absence, locked date, public holiday, etc.

- `Booking`
- `PublicHoliday`
- `NonWorkingDay`
- `LockedDate`
- `Birthday`
- `WorkAnniversary`

fromTime.description:
Use in conjuction with the From to denote the part of day that the leave request starts.
AM: Starts in the morning of the day.
PM: Starts at lunchtime of the day.
Number: Alternatively, for hourly bookings, you can specify a time, expressed as minutes since midnight.

toTime.description:
Use in conjuction with the To to denote the part of day that the leave request ends.
AM: Ends at the end of the the morning (lunchtime).
PM: Ends at the end of the day.
Number: Alternatively, for hourly bookings, you can specify a time, expressed as minutes since midnight.

- `Department`
- `Everyone`

suppressEmails.description:
If you are an admin, you can request that emails are suppressed for this request.
This will prevent any leave request emails from being sent when the request is processed.

override.description:
If you are an admin, and the booking would be rejected because it exceeds the max-off limit for this department,
setting override allows you to make the booking despite that limit.

bookAsRequestee.description:
If you are an admin, set this to true to make the leave request as though it were being made by the requestee (the person you are booking for).
This ensures the normal approval flow will happen.
The default is false - leave requests will be booked by the admin user account making the API call.

overrideLockedDays.description:
If you are an admin, and the booking would be rejected because it covers locked dates
setting OverrideLockedDays allows you to make the booking ignoring existing locks.

overrideAccruedAllowance.description:
If you are an admin, and the booking would be rejected because it doesn't have enough accrued allowance, but has enough annual allowance.
setting OverrideAccruedAllowance allows you to make the booking ignoring accrued allowance.

attachmentId.description: If you've added an attachment, assign it to this booking by passing the ID here.

UTC equivalent of the actual start of the booking period, adjusted for the organisation timezone and user work schedule.
For daily bookings this reflects the start of the working day/period.

startType.description:
Morning - Booked for the morning of the start date
Afternoon - Booked after the morning of the start date (starts at lunchtime)
Hours - This is an hourly booking, use the time in the Start.

- `Morning`
- `Afternoon`
- `Hours`

endDate.description: End of the holiday. Use in conjunction with the end type to determine the holiday end

endType.description:
Used to define the time the holiday ends:
Morning - Ends after the morning of the last day (lunchtime)
Afternoon - Ends at the end of the last day (whole day booked)
Hours - This is an hourly booking, use the time in the Start.

- `Morning`
- `Afternoon`
- `Hours`

Why the user could not be added.

- `2` — **Failed**: The user could not be created. Common causes are a departmentId that belongs to another organisation, and a recently created account that has hit its temporary user limit.
- `3` — **InvalidValue**: A supplied value was rejected: an email address already in use by another Timetastic user, an email address on a blocked domain, a blank first or last name, or a start date outside the current or next leave year.
- `5` — **NotPermitted**: You are not allowed to add users to that department.
- `8` — **InvalidEmail**: The email address failed format validation.

- `2` — **InvalidValue**: The request contained an invalid value (e.g. attempting to delete a department that still has users).

errorStatus.description:
Why the user could not be edited.

- `2` — **Failed**: The edit was rejected; errorMessage says why. Common causes are: the user is archived and must be unarchived first, the email address is already in use, removing the last remaining administrator, un-admining yourself, clearing the email address of a user who needs one, making a user both an admin and a director, setting admin or director on a user with no email address, and a start date outside the current or next leave year.
- `6` — **NotPermitted**: Returned with a 401. The user ID does not exist or belongs to another organisation, or you tried to set a Pro-only field without a Timetastic Pro account.
- `8` — **InvalidEmail**: The email address failed format validation.

tags.name: Absences
tags.description:
Get upcoming absences; Bookings, non working days, public holidays or other Timetastic Events like Locked Dates, Birthdays or Work Anniversaries
            
Use this endpoint if you're updating your own dashboard, internal calendar or 3rd party app and only want to know what's coming up soon without querying multiple endpoints in our API

tags.name: Departments
tags.description: Access all the departments at your organisation.

tags.name: Holidays
tags.description: View, book, or action holidays at your organisation. Using the ```holidays``` endpoint, you can query for all types of leave bookings in Timetastic. You can also use this endpoint to update (approve or decline) holidays and to request new time off. Note: **Holidays** in the context of this API actually refer to any absence. We apologize for any confusion, but the API was first built in 2014 and to update the endpoints would risk a large amount of breaking changes.
